description: A data table spec is valid when columns are fully defined, pagination is declared for large datasets, selection and bulk action state is explicit, every table has a loading and empty state, sortable columns have sort definitions, and destructive bulk actions require confirmation.

rules.description: data-table-spec.json must exist with table_id (string), columns (array), and pagination (object with pageSize). Tables without a spec cannot be validated.
Every column must declare id, label, and field. Columns without these fields cannot be rendered or bound to API responses.
pagination.pageSize must be a number greater than 0. A zero or missing page size produces empty or infinite page requests.
When estimatedRowCount > 25 or pagination.required:true, pageSize must be between 1 and 100. Rendering thousands of rows without pagination degrades performance.
When selectable:true, selectionState must declare maxSelection and bulkActions. Tables that allow selection without declaring selection limits create unpredictable multi-select behavior.
Every table must declare loadingState as skeleton, spinner, or overlay. Tables that fetch data without a loading state appear broken or frozen.
Every table must declare emptyState with a non-empty message. A blank table with no explanation creates confusion about whether the data is missing or the feature is broken.
Any column with sortable:true must be listed in spec.sortableColumns or spec.sorts. Marking a column sortable without an API sort binding creates a broken UI interaction.
Any bulkAction with destructive:true must declare a confirmation object with message. Destructive batch operations without confirmation can irrecoverably destroy data.
All column ids must be unique within the spec. Duplicate column ids cause conflicting sort/filter bindings and broken column visibility toggles.
